Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan instructed by ASM Khalequzzaman Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants.

Md. Motiruddin Mondal @ Matiar Rahman Mondal & others ------ Appellants
Vs.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 23.08.2001 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1998 of 1999)
full_judgment:
M.M. Ruhul Amin J.: This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 23.08.2001 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1998 of 1999 making the Rule absolute.

2. Short facts are that the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos. 1, 2 and 3 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 1005 of 1984 for declaration of title in the first schedule land measuring 70 acres. The appellant and the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Naogaon were impleaded as defendant and proforma defendant respectively. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that 'Ka' and 'Kha' schedule suit land originally belonged to Raja Amiya Narayan Sannayal of Puria raj Estate. Khailash Chandra Mahantau and Ishwar Chandra Mahantu took pattan of the suit lands from the Putia Raj Estate.

<u>3. Subsequently they settled the suit lands in favour of the plaintiff respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and one Boyezuddin Mollah by way of korfa pattan on 15th Kartick, 1357 B.S. The S.A. and R.S. record of rights being S.A. Khatian No. 384 and R.S. Khatian No. 17 were, prepared and correctly published in the name, of the plaintiff respondent Nos.1 and 2 and Boyezuddin. Boyezuddin possessed the 'Kha' schedule land by cultivating it. After the death of Boyezuddin his heirs transferred the entire share to the plaintiff respondent Nos. 1 and 2 by a kabala dated 12.01.1977. The C.S. record of rights of the 'Kha' schedule land was prepared and published in the name of Mudhu Lal Bhowmick, Jadu Lal Bhowmick, Ram Ballav Bhowmick, Chandra Kumar Bhowmick and Jageswar Bhowmick as tenants under the landlord. They surrendered their land orally in favour of Zaminder long before the acquisition of Zamindary by the Government. The plaintiff respondent by way of korfa settlement and by kabala dated 12.01.1977 have been owing and possessing the land in exercise   of right, title and interest. On Magh 25, 1389 B.S. the defendants disclosed that the R.S. Khatian of 'Kha' schedule property was prepared in the name of their father and they wanted to take possession   of the land. Accordingly the plaintiff was constrained to file the present suit.</u>

4. The defendant's case is that the suit land of C.S. Khatian No. 422 belonged to Mudhu Lal Bhowmick and others who were C.S. recorded tenants and it was transferred in favour of Uzir Mondal, the father of the defendants by unregistered deed dated 11 Poush, 1353 B.S. Thereafter, the defendants changed the nature of the suit property by excavating a pond and have been in possession of the suit property for more than twenty years. But due to their illness they could not take step to have their names recorded in the S.A. record. After the death of their father the defendants inherited the suit land. The plaintiffs and Boyezuddin who never possessed the suit property collusively got their names recorded in the S.A. an R.S. records.

5. The learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Naogaon decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff respondents. The defendant preferred Title Appeal No. 184 of 1997 before the learned District Judge, Naogaon who by his judgment and decree dated 15.06.1999 allowed the appeal. Against the judgment of reversal the plaintiff preferred Civil Revision No. 1998 of 1999 before the High Court Division and upon hearing the Rule was made absolute and the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court was set aside.

6. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in reversing the decision of the appellate court in view of the finding of the appellate court that the plaintiff respondents failed to rebut the presumption of the R.S. record of rights which has been finally published in the names of the defendant and the further submission that the S.A. record of rights and R.S. Khatian No. 17 have been published in the names of the plaintiff respondents without any basis in view of the fact that the case of korfa settlement has not been proved  and hence the kabala executed by the heirs of one of the korfa tenants has not been acted upon and the further submission that the appellate court found that the S.A. record of right and R.S. Khatian No. 17 in the names of the plaintiff respondents have no basis but the High Court Division committed an error of law in reversing the decision of the appellate court in revisional jurisdiction.

7. We have heard Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Counsel for the appellants and Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Counsel for respondent Nos. 1-3 and perused the judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers.

8. It is not disputed that the suit land belonged to Modhu Lal Bhowmick and other under landlord Amiya Narayan Sannayal of Putia Raj Estate and C.S. Khatian No. 422 of Mouza Borpai, P.S. Manda was prepared and finally published accordingly. The plaintiff’s case is that Modhu Lal Bhomick and others surrendered their land orally in favour of the landlord and thereafter Khailash Chandra Mahantau and Ishwar Chandra Mahantu took settlement of the suit lands from the Zaminder. Subsequently Khailash Chandra Mahantau and Ishwar Chandra Mahantu settled the suit lands in favour of the plaintiff respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and one Boyezuddin Mollah by way of korfa pattan on Kartick 15, 1357 B.S. and the S.A. and R.S. record were correctly prepared and finally published in the names of the plaintiff respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and Boyezuddin. After the death of Boyezuddin his heirs transferred the entire share in favour of the plaintiff respondent Nos. 1 and 2 by a kabala dated 12.01.1977. The case of the contesting defendant is that their predecessor Uzir Mondal got the land by unregistered deed dated 11th Poush, 1353 B.S. from Modhu Lal Bhowmick and others and after their purchase they changed the nature of the suit property by excavating a pond and have been in possession of the suit property for more than twenty years. But due to the illness of their father they could not take step to have their names recorded in the S.A. record.

9. It is undisputed that S.A. record was prepared in the name of the defendant rather same was prepared in the name of the plaintiffs.

10. It is not disputed that A.S. Khatian No. 17 in respect of the suit land was prepared in the name of the plaintiffs earlier but later on R.S. Khatian No. 82 for the suit land was also prepared in the name of the defendants.

11. The trial court held that the plaintiffs could not file any pattan nama in their favour granted by Khailash Chandra Mahantau and Ishwar Chandra Mahantu on Kartick 15, 1357 B.S. The trial court accepted the contention of the plaintiffs that those were lost on the way while going to the Court from their dwelling house. G.D. entry was accordingly lodged by the plaintiffs at the local police station and the trial court accepted the contention of the plaintiffs that those papers were lost, so the plaintiffs could not file those. The trial court found that on the basis of the S.A. record prepared in the name of the plaintiffs   they paid rent to the Government and produced 17 dakhilas before the Court. The trial court further observed that if the plaintiffs were not in possession of the suit land there was no reason for preparation of S.A. and R.S. records in their names and there was also no reason for them to pay rent for the suit land by 17 dakhilas.

12. The trial court further held that the plaintiffs filed two dakhilas granted by the landlords in their favour. But in the dakhilas the plot number and khatian number were not mentioned but those were granted by the Putia Raj estate and there is no evidence on record that the plaintiffs were tenants in respect of other lands under Putia Raj Estate. The trial court did not believe the defendant's contention that during S.A. record their predecessor Uzir Mondal was ill and as such could not get land recorded in their names. The trial court found that defendant's two elder brothers, Mahir and Lahir were aged 28 and 20 at the time of S.A. operation. So according to defendant's own case if their father was ill at the time of S.A. operation the two elder brothers who were adult at that time could take step for recording their name in the S.A. Khatian.

13. The defendants' case is that his father got the suit land by unregistered deed of the year 1353 B.S. from C.S. tenants Modhu Lal Bhowmick and others. The unregistered document was lost from the Court and as a result the heirs of Modhu Lal Bhowmick and others subsequently on 25.11.1987 executed another document in favour of the defendant and from the recitals of the subsequent document, it appears that their predecessor-in-interest transferred the suit land in favour of Uzir Mondal, the predecessor of the defendant on 11th Poush, 1353 B.S. orally. The Court while disposing of an application for temporary injunction filed by the plaintiffs held that unregistered document filed by the defendant was not reliable because there were several erasing and over writings in the document and the same was newly created for the purpose of the present suit.

<u>14. The trial court further opined that the unregistered document was removed from the Court's record and the presumption is that the defendant did it as by order dated 16.03.1986, the Court while disposing of temporary injunction matter remarked that there were several erasing and over writings in the document and the same was newly created for the purpose of the present suit and the above observations are against the defendant.</u>

15. It is the definite case of the defendant that after the purchase by his father by unregistered document they changed the nature of the suit property by excavating a pond in the suit land. From the C.S. Khatian No. 422, it is clear that Plot No. 442 was recorded as pond in the finally published C.S. Khatian.

16. Therefore, the question of excavating pond by the defendant after their purchase by unregistered deed (initially) and then oral purchase (the 2nd case) in 1353 B.S. is a math.

<u>17. The trial court further observed that the D.W.1, Md. Jahiruddin Mondal in his evidence stated that his father Uzir Mondal excavated a pond in the suit land in 1349 B.S. whereas in the written statement they claimed to have purchased by unregistered deed (initial, case) and subsequent case oral the suit land in 1353 B.S. So it is difficult to believe the so-called either by unregistered deed or oral purchase of the defendant in 1353 B.S. as because it has been claimed purchasing the land they excavated a pond in the suit land in 1349 B.S.</u>

<u>18. The trail court further held that the defendant produced only one dakhila of the year 1991 and they could not file any other dakhila. It appears that the appellate court while allowing the appeal did not reverse the findings of the trial court on material points. The High Court Division while making the Rule absolute it appears took into consideration the material evidence on record including evidence of P.Ws. and 6 and D.Ws. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 and the relevant documents and held that the trial court took into consideration the documentary and oral evidence on record and recorded its reasoning in support of its findings and decision and the judgment of the trial court is well reasoned. On the other hand, the appellate court did not discuss the evidence on record properly and did not controvert the findings of the trial court with reference to documentary and oral evidence on record.</u>

<u>19. The High Court Division further held that the judgment of the Court of appeal suffers from defect of misreading of evidence and non-consideration of materials of materials on record.</u>

<u>20. In the circumstances, we are of the view that the High Court Division considered the materials on record in proper perspective and after assigning cogent reasons arrived at a correct conclusion and hence does not require interference by us.</u>

<u>21. The appeal is dismissed with costs.</u>

End.
